title: Classical ML II (applied) | Agents & tool use
objectives: Cover the applied ML problems big-tech DS roles face. Build an agent and know when an agent is the wrong tool.
exercise: Build a 'data analyst agent' with two tools, run_sql (DuckDB, read-only) and plot, that answers questions over your Week 1 dataset. Log traces, then run a 30-question eval with pass/fail checks on SQL correctness.
resources: Designing Machine Learning Systems (Huyen, 2022): features & training data chapters

cards.q: Why standardise features before k-means and PCA?
choices: Both use distances/variance, so large-scale features (e.g. amount in $) would dominate

cards.q: k-means implicitly assumes clusters that are…
choices: Roughly spherical, similar size, separable by distance to centroid
cards.explain: For arbitrary shapes, consider DBSCAN or GMMs.

cards.q: PCA's first principal component is…
choices: The direction of maximum variance in the (centred) data
The feature with the largest mean

cards.q: A common heuristic for choosing k in k-means?
choices: Elbow in within-cluster SSE and/or silhouette score, validated by business usefulness

cards.q: Eigenvalues of a 3-feature covariance matrix: 6, 3, 1. What share of variance does PC1 explain (%)?
Why split recommendation into candidate retrieval and ranking stages?
choices: Cheap retrieval narrows millions of items to hundreds; an expensive ranker then scores only those within the latency budget

cards.q: A two-tower model…
choices: Embeds users and items separately, so item embeddings can be precomputed and searched with ANN
Scores every user–item pair with cross features

cards.q: Cold start for a new merchant with no interactions. Mitigation?
choices: Content/metadata features (cuisine, price, location) and exploration boosts

cards.q: NDCG rewards…
choices: Relevant items placed higher in the list (graded relevance, log-discounted by position)
Only whether any relevant item appears

cards.q: Feedback loop risk in recommenders?
choices: The model only learns from items it chose to show, reinforcing popularity bias

cards.q: Why is random k-fold CV wrong for time series?
choices: It trains on the future to predict the past (leakage) and breaks temporal dependence; use rolling-origin backtests

cards.q: Spot the leak: forecasting daily volume using a 7-day centred moving average as a feature.
choices: The centred window uses future days; use trailing windows only

cards.q: Simple strong baseline for daily transaction volume with weekly seasonality?
choices: Seasonal naive: same weekday last week

cards.q: Why is MAPE problematic for low-volume series?
choices: Division by small or zero actuals explodes the error; consider MAE, WAPE or sMAPE

cards.q: Forecast for Hari Raya / Chinese New Year spikes. Best approach?
choices: Explicit holiday features (moving dates) learned from past years

cards.q: Labels arrive 60 days late (chargebacks). How does that affect training and monitoring?
cards.answer: Training: the most recent 60 days are unlabelled or look like false negatives, so exclude immature data or model label maturity, which means the model learns from older patterns. Monitoring: you can't measure precision/recall in real time. Use proxies (score distribution drift, alert rates, early signals like customer disputes, manual review outcomes) and backfill true performance later.
rubric: Recent data immature → exclude or treat carefully
Real-time performance unknown → proxy metrics / drift / review labels

cards.q: Isolation Forest flags anomalies because…
choices: Anomalies are isolated in fewer random splits (short path lengths)

cards.q: Fraudsters adapt after your model launches. This is…
choices: Adversarial concept drift: monitor and retrain frequently

cards.q: SHAP values explain…
choices: Each feature's additive contribution to one prediction relative to a baseline

cards.q: Uplift modelling targets…
choices: Users whose outcome changes most because of treatment (persuadables), not just who's likely to convert

cards.q: A monthly report with fixed steps: workflow or agent?
cards.explain: Predefined code paths are cheaper, more predictable and easier to test.

cards.q: Anthropic's definition: an agent is a system where…
choices: The LLM dynamically directs its own process and tool use
Several LLM calls run in a fixed order

cards.q: When is an agent appropriate?
choices: Open-ended tasks where the number of steps can't be predicted and you can trust/verify the model's choices

cards.q: Main costs of agents vs workflows?
choices: Higher latency and cost, compounding errors, harder to test

cards.q: The 'augmented LLM' building block is…
choices: An LLM enhanced with retrieval, tools and memory

cards.q: Which pattern fits 'generate SQL, run it, critique the result, revise'?
Classify a support ticket, then send it to a specialised prompt per category. Pattern?
Run three independent guardrail checks simultaneously and combine them. Pattern?
A central LLM breaks a task into subtasks it decides at runtime, delegates them, then synthesises. Pattern?
Outline → check outline meets criteria → write document. Pattern?
Name MCP's three server primitives.
cards.answer: Tools (model-invoked actions), Resources (data/context the application can read), Prompts (reusable templates the user can invoke).

cards.q: MCP messages use which protocol format?
What problem does MCP solve?
choices: A standard way to connect any AI app to any tool/data source instead of N×M bespoke integrations

cards.q: How should tool descriptions from an untrusted MCP server be treated?
choices: As untrusted input: they can carry prompt injection, so review servers and scope permissions
As user messages with full authority

cards.q: For your capstone, a read-only SQL lookup exposed via MCP is a…
cards.explain: A static schema document could be exposed as a Resource.

cards.q: Why evaluate the tool-call trajectory, not just the final answer?
choices: A right answer can come from a wrong or unsafe path (lucky guess, extra costly calls, risky actions), and trajectory errors pinpoint what to fix

cards.q: Your data agent's run_sql tool should connect with…
choices: A read-only role scoped to allowed schemas, plus query timeouts and row limits
The same credentials as the app

cards.q: A pass/fail check for 'SQL correctness' in your agent eval should compare…
choices: The query's result set to a reference result (not the SQL text)
Whether it ran without error only

cards.q: Main cost risk of multi-agent systems?
choices: Token usage multiplies across agents; use them only when the parallelism/value justifies it

cards.q: Stopping condition every agent loop needs?
choices: Max steps/budget limits plus a clear completion criterion
